Agency vs Consultancy vs Advisor vs Fractional: Explained

Guidelowob research

By lowob · 2 February 2026 · Updated 16 November 2026 · 8-minute read · Strategy

Agencies sell execution, consultancies sell answers, advisors sell judgment over time, and fractional executives sell part-time ownership of a function. Each is paid differently, and the payment tells you what you are really buying. The four markets are shifting at once: Lightcast counts at least 34,000 US workers with "fractional" in their title, up 265% since 2019, and Gartner found 22% of CMOs say generative AI has reduced their reliance on agencies for creativity and strategy. Match the purchase to what you are missing, and insist on a paid, scoped first step from anyone offering more than one.

Companies looking for marketing help are usually offered four different things under overlapping names. Knowing which one you are buying saves months.

The four, defined by what you receive

An agency sells execution. You receive work product: campaigns run, media bought, content produced, programmes operated. The agency staffs the work with its own people and tools, and you review outputs rather than doing them. Agencies are paid on retainers, project fees, a percentage of media spend, or, less often, on performance. It is a large, established market: US Census Bureau data show advertising agencies with employer payrolls earned about $64 billion in 2022, and public relations agencies about $20 billion.

A consultancy sells answers. You receive analysis and recommendations: what the market looks like, what the plan should be, how the organisation should be structured. Consultancies are paid by project or by the day, and the deliverable is usually a document and a presentation. Whether anyone acts on it is your problem. Source Global Research, which tracks firms with more than 50 consultants, expects technology consulting alone to pass $400 billion in global revenue in 2026, and found two-thirds of buyers it surveyed expect consulting prices to rise.

An advisor sells judgment over time. You receive access to a person with relevant experience who helps you make decisions as they come up. Advisors are paid a modest monthly fee, equity, or both, and the deliverable is the quality of the decisions you make with them in the room. They rarely do the work. The equity norms are well documented: the Founder Institute's FAST agreement, a standard one-page advisor template, suggests 0.25% of a seed-stage company for an advisor who meets monthly, vesting over two years.

A fractional executive sells a part-time leader. You receive someone who takes ownership of a function for a fixed number of days per week, manages people and vendors, and is accountable for results. Fractional leaders are paid a monthly fee scaled to their time, and the deliverable is a function that runs. Go Fractional, a marketplace, reports that fractional CMOs on its platform averaged 27 hours a week over the 90 days to mid-2026.

Where the confusion comes from

The names have drifted. Agencies call themselves consultancies because it sounds senior. Consultancies offer "implementation support" to keep the engagement going. Advisors get pulled into doing work because they are close and capable. Fractional executives are asked to be advisors when the budget shrinks, and advisors are asked to be fractional when the company needs hands.

Each drift produces a mismatch between what is being paid for and what is being received. The most common failure is hiring an advisor, paying advisor rates, and expecting execution.

Two market shifts are widening the overlap. The first is AI. Gartner's 2025 survey of 402 marketing leaders found 39% planned to cut agency budgets and 22% said generative AI had already reduced their reliance on external agencies for creativity and strategy. When drafts get cheaper, every provider starts describing itself as strategic. Our piece on why judgment is becoming the marketing moat covers the effect in detail.

The second is the growth of fractional work. Lightcast, a labour-market analytics firm, found US fractional job postings more than doubled in 2025, and that 97% of fractional postings in 2026 came from small and medium-sized companies. Marketing and PR made up 10% of postings, behind finance at 46%. A growing supply of part-time leaders means more people offering a mix of advice and ownership, often without saying which.

The most common failure is hiring an advisor, paying advisor rates, and expecting execution.

How to choose

Ask what you are missing.

If you know what to do and lack the hands to do it, you need execution: an agency, or a fractional leader with a team.

If you do not know what to do and the question is large enough to justify a study, you need a consultancy, and you should budget for the execution that follows separately.

If you know roughly what to do but face decisions weekly that would benefit from someone who has made them before, you need an advisor.

If the function has no leader and you cannot yet justify a full-time one, you need a fractional executive.

What you are missingBuyWatch for
Hands, with a clear planAgency, or fractional leader with a teamScope that drifts toward what the provider sells best
The plan itself, on a large questionConsultancyNo budget set aside for execution
A second view on recurring decisionsAdvisorBeing asked to do work at advisor rates
A leader for a functionFractional executiveToo few days to manage people properly

The table works only if you can state the gap in a sentence. A go-to-market strategy is the usual place that sentence comes from: if you cannot name the buyer, the offer and the route to market, you are missing the plan, and buying hands first will be expensive.

The hybrid, and its condition

Some firms combine advice with execution: a short diagnostic that leads into building and running the thing that was recommended. That is what we do. The advantage is that the recommendation is made by the people who will have to deliver it, which tends to produce recommendations that are achievable.

The condition that makes a hybrid honest is a paid, scoped first step with a defined end, so that the advice is not a free sales pitch for the execution. A one-week diagnostic that costs money and produces a written answer is advice. A free proposal is marketing.

The wider market supports the caution. The European Association of Communications Agencies surveyed 412 agencies in 2025 and found the average new-business pitch cost an agency about €43,800 in people and expenses. That cost does not disappear. It is recovered in the fees of the engagement that follows, which is why free strategy tends to recommend whatever the provider sells. Our explainer on what a distribution diagnostic is sets out what a paid first step should contain.

Questions to ask any of them

Five questions sort the four quickly:

  1. What exactly will I receive, and when? Work product, a document, access or a running function.
  2. Who does the work, and how senior are they? The person who sold it, or someone you have not met.
  3. How are you paid, and what does that reward? Time, spend, outcomes or the relationship continuing.
  4. What happens to my accounts, data and relationships if we stop? The answer shows who owns the asset.
  5. What is not included? The profitable part of many engagements sits just outside the original description.

Clear answers to those five questions tell you which of the four you are actually talking to, whatever the website says. Our guide to how marketing services are priced goes further on question three, and Build it to run without you on question four.

Agencies sell execution, consultancies sell answers, advisors sell judgment, and fractional leaders sell part-time ownership. Match the purchase to the gap, and insist on a paid, scoped first step from anyone offering more than one.

lowob takeaways

  • Buy by what you receive. Work product, a recommendation, better decisions or a running function are four different purchases.
  • Read the fee for the product. How someone is paid shows what they are really selling.
  • Do not expect execution at advisor rates. It is the most common mismatch and the easiest to prevent.
  • Ask for a paid first step from hybrids. A free proposal is marketing; a paid one-week diagnostic with a written answer is advice.

Common questions

What is the difference between an agency and a consultancy?

An agency sells execution: campaigns run, media bought, content produced. A consultancy sells answers: analysis and recommendations, usually delivered as a document, and whether anyone acts on it is your problem.

What is a fractional executive?

A senior leader who owns a function, such as marketing or finance, for a fixed number of days a week, manages people and vendors, and is accountable for results. They are usually paid a monthly fee scaled to their time.

When should a company hire a fractional executive instead of an advisor?

Hire a fractional executive when a function has no leader and you cannot yet justify a full-time one. Hire an advisor when you know roughly what to do but face weekly decisions that benefit from someone who has made them before.

How much equity does a startup advisor usually get?

The Founder Institute's FAST template suggests 0.25% at seed for an advisor who meets monthly and up to 1% at pre-seed for a more involved expert, typically vesting over two years. Terms vary, so treat these as reference points.

Sources and notes

  • Gartner, 2025 CMO Spend Survey, 12 May 2025. Analyst survey of 402 marketing leaders in North America, the UK and Europe; mostly larger companies.
  • Lightcast, The rise of fractional leadership, 20 August 2026. Labour-market analytics vendor using its own job-posting and profile data; US posting counts are small in absolute terms.
  • Go Fractional, 2026 State of Fractional Work, updated 9 June 2026. Marketplace vendor report from its own platform data and a survey of 213 fractional professionals; not representative of the whole market.
  • Consultancy.uk, Global technology consulting market to surpass $400 billion in 2026, 19 December 2025. Reports Source Global Research forecasts and buyer survey; covers firms with more than 50 consultants and excludes outsourcing.
  • Founder Institute, FAST Agreement, Version 3, July 2026. Standard advisor template from an accelerator; suggested equity ranges, not market data.
  • FRED, Total Revenue for Advertising Agencies and Public Relations Agencies, US Census Bureau Service Annual Survey. Employer firms only; latest year shown is 2022.
  • EACA, Europe's billion euro pitching problem, 11 June 2025. Trade-association survey of 412 member agencies; self-reported costs.

Before your next call with an outside provider, write down in one sentence what you are missing: hands, a plan, a second view or a leader. Then ask them the five questions above and check whether their answers match the sentence.
